Defects, and the ones that turned out not to be
### 3.1 The BatchNorm double-update: measured, bounded, and NOT a lever
src/train.py:496-499 warns that gradient checkpointing double-updates BatchNorm running statistics, and that "Training is unaffected;
no Kaggle fold does (MEASURED, §1: armc1–armc4 and fold0–fold4 all record grad_checkpoint=False/absent).
So the deployed 22 mixes two regimes: 4 members checkpointed (armb0, armb0.swa, armc0, armc0.swa) and 18 not.
Three measurements settle what that costs.
(a) The double-update is 67 of 69 BN layers, not all of them. MEASURED — reading num_batches_tracked out of the state dicts:
The two stem/head BatchNorms sit outside the checkpointed blocks and are updated once;
every BN inside encoder.blocks is updated twice.
A non-checkpointed member shows a single value (armc1, armc3: {10434}).
This refines T022: the effect is per-layer, not global, and the un-doubled pair is exactly the two layers timm leaves outside set_grad_checkpointing.
only the estimator window moves. INFERRED, model stated: PyTorch's BN update is running ← (1−m)·running + m·batch with m = 0.1 (timm leaves the default).
Applying it twice per optimizer step gives an effective m' = 1 − (1−0.1)² = 0.19.
Both are exponential moving averages of the same batch-statistic distribution, so they share an expectation;
what differs is the effective window, 1/m = 10 batches against 1/m' = 5.3 batches.
At the 10,434–20,880 steps these checkpoints record, both are converged many hundreds of time constants past initialisation.
The difference is therefore a variance difference in the final buffer, not a bias.
(c) And the measured buffer difference is smaller than the fold-to-fold difference. MEASURED, across the 69 BN layers of each member:
The checkpointed member sits inside the spread of the two non-checkpointed ones on both statistics.
This is not a controlled comparison — fold and venue move with the regime — but it is the comparison that would show an outlier if the regime dominated, and it does not.

(d) The controlled answer already exists and agrees. READ — PROGRESS.md:3372-3399, T022 Gate D at --bs 2 --grad-checkpoint: Δrho −0.0115 (local better) against the pair's own band ±0.0112, r = 0.8308.
Verdict recorded there: "NOT EQUIVALENT at bs=2 either — but marginally, and in the harmless direction."
Verdict: NULL as a lever. The regimes are distinguishable at 1.03× the band, in the direction that favours the members we already trust, and the buffer difference is below fold noise.
Mixing them in the blend is diversity, not error.

The one arithmetically clean fix — set momentum = 1 − sqrt(1−0.1) = 0.0513 on the 67 doubled layers, which restores an effective 0.1 exactly and invents no new constant, since it is derived from the existing one — is ~4 lines and is bounded above by Gate D's 0.0115 rho, almost all of which is attributable to fold and venue rather than to BN.
### 3.2 What I checked and found clean
Recording nulls, because a null that is written down is not re-checked:

- Epoch propagation to the workers. train.py:531 sets train_ds.epoch = ep before the iterator is built, and no DataLoader in the file sets persistent_workers (:445-452), so the fork carries the new epoch.
The mirror/rotate stream at dataset.py:342 is genuinely re-drawn each epoch.
- The intensity window under --adjacent. dicom_io.py:513 computes np.percentile(vol, [1.0, 99.0]) at line 513, and the packing that adds neighbour channels happens at :517-545, after.
The docstring's claim that the window comes from the centre slices alone is exact.
- tta.py's two round-1 bugs. Both fixed under T039;
the current apply_view (:265-277) transforms all three channels via reshape(bsc,...) and mirror_bag (:223) flips dims=[0,1] on the slice axis.
- The blend arithmetic. tta.blend:311-321 divides by the weight that actually landed, per study and per label;

the kernel's member mean (rsna-knee-submit.py:281-288) accumulates psum/pcount so the result is a flat mean over all members regardless of layout grouping, which the comment proves is identical to blending first because the view weights do not depend on the predicted values.
Clean, and the linearity argument holds.
- select_ckpts (:107-…) fails loudly on a pattern that matches nothing.
- The PRIORS fallback (:96, used at :163/:373) never fired: MEASURED, the v16 run log says every scored study used all 22 members.
### 3.3 The deployed ensemble is at the layout cap, and that blocks T007
The layout key is (slices, size, seqs, adjacent) (rsna-knee-submit.py:209, :273-275) and MAX_LAYOUTS is 2 (:85).
The deployed ensemble already occupies both slots. A --seqs 2 member from T007 has layout (12, 320, 2, True) — a third layout — so rsna-knee-submit.py:235 would SystemExit on it.

pm/tasks/T007-sequence-diversity-clean.md contains no occurrence of "layout", "MAX_LAYOUTS", "deploy" or "submit" (MEASURED, grep in appendix A), and pm/tasks/T028-config-for-the-family.md:444-445 says only that the cap "does not need raising" for T028's case.

Three ways out, none free, and the choice is a submission-side decision: raise RSNA_MAX_LAYOUTS to 3 and pay a third full pass over the test data (the kernel prints ~67 min for two passes at 22×3, so INFERRED ~+30 min);
or drop the ten fold? members, which frees the slot and unlocks three TTA views (§3.4) but costs ten of twenty-two members;
This should be recorded on T007 before its fold is judged, because "the screen adopted" and "the member is deployable" are not the same question here.

### 3.5 Three hyperparameters with no CLI at all — the one real new lever
This is the strongest new find in the lane, and it is the direct descendant of the --layer-decay discovery rather than a repeat of it.
READ — src/train.py:458-462 constructs the model with five arguments:
dropout is not among them, so it takes KneeMIL's default 0.3 (src/model.py:169).
Weight decay is the literal 1e-4, written four times (train.py:268, :276, :284, :289) and reachable by no flag.
And there is no way to set the encoder's learning rate independently of the head's.
(the recipe column is READ from docs/research/0902b/lane6-single-model-gap.md — the head's Dropout(0.2) at :174, the LR/weight-decay rows at :182-184.)
Why --layer-decay does not substitute for --encoder-lr. MEASURED — timm assigns 24 distinct layer levels to tf_efficientnet_b2, split into 48 parameter groups covering 299/299 encoder tensors:
A geometric ramp cannot produce a flat encoder LR at 0.1× the head.
The value whose median encoder scale lands nearest the recipe's 0.1 is ≈0.82, and even there the spread across groups is 0.006 to 1.0 — a 170× range where the recipe has a 1× range.
The shape the public recipe uses is not expressible in our CLI.

Partly already registered. pm/STATE.md's NOW block (2026-09-02 10:25Z) records a pre-launch CPU check of the same object — "timm finds 23 layer levels in tf_efficientnet_b2 → 48 groups, lr_scale 1e-5…1.0 … the param-weighted mean encoder LR is 1.35e-4, only 2.2× below the head … the stem is frozen in effect".
That is the same measurement weighted by parameter count rather than by group, and the two agree.

What is new here is the consequence: not "0.6 is a graded cut" (registered) but "no value of --layer-decay reproduces the recipe, so T042 cannot answer the question it was written to answer, whatever its verdict", plus the table that says which value to pick if a graded cut is what is wanted (0.85–0.90, where nothing freezes).

The fix is small. An --encoder-lr flag is one add_argument plus one branch in build_optimizer that puts model.encoder.parameters() in a group at args.encoder_lr and everything else at args.lr — the enc/rest split at train.py:282-285 already exists and is reused verbatim.
~8 lines. --weight-decay is one flag replacing four literals;
--dropout is one flag threaded to KneeMIL.
All three default to today's values, so every measured number keeps its meaning — the house rule at train.py:751-754.

The pre-registered shape, if the orchestrator wants it, is the same one lane 6 wrote for S1 with the axis corrected:
against outputs/t028/armC_fold0.oof.csv, same fold, seed and split-seed.

That is the public recipe's actual shape — a flat low encoder LR under a full-LR head, warmed up — where --layer-decay 0.6 is a geometric ramp that freezes the stem and leaves the late encoder, which holds most of the parameters, at full LR.

The two are close to opposites, so a null from T042 does not close the lever, and this lane's recommendation is that T042's verdict be recorded as answering "graded encoder LR decay", not "encoder LR too high", whichever way it lands.
If a graded cut is wanted anyway, §3.5's table says 0.85 to 0.90 is the band where nothing freezes: median encoder scale 0.155 to 0.298, minimum 0.024 to 0.089, zero groups below 1e-6.

## Appendix B — what this lane does not establish
It does not measure any lever. Zero GPU was spent by design.
Every magnitude in §5 is INFERRED or borrowed from lane 6;
the only MEASURED numbers here are code facts, checkpoint contents and the timm layer-decay spectrum.
It does not establish that --encoder-lr 3e-5 helps. It establishes that the recipe's shape is not expressible today and that --layer-decay 0.6 is a different intervention.
Whether either helps is unmeasured on our recipe.
The BatchNorm comparison in §3.1(c) is not controlled. armc0 differs from armc1/armc3 in fold and venue as well as in regime.
The controlled answer is Gate D's, and it is quoted rather than reproduced.
It does not price the third layout. The ~30 min figure in §3.3 is INFERRED by scaling the kernel's own two-pass estimate;
no third-layout run exists and the rerun ceiling above 48 M·V is still unmeasured from above.
It does not audit src/weak_labels.py, src/manifest.py, src/targets.py, src/mirror.py, src/metric.py or scripts/smoke_test.py line by line. The audit followed the flags and the deployed path;
a defect confined to the labeling or manifest side would not have been reached.
In particular scripts/smoke_test.py (3,634 lines) was not run — the lane brief forbids it, since it touches CUDA and would defer the queued fold — so nothing here is backed by the test suite.
It does not check whether the fold? members' absent adjacent is correct. Those ten predate the flag;
whether they should be retired is T034's question, not this lane's.
--seed diversity is a hypothesis, not a finding. That all 30 checkpoints share seed=0 is MEASURED;
that this explains the flat return curve past k≈12 is not tested and would cost a fold.
The add_argument enumeration covers src/.py and scripts/.py only. scripts/llm_label/ and notebooks/ were not enumerated;
the labeling harness is out of scope per the standing prohibition on new labeling passes.
